title: The Two-Plate Reckoning
subtitle: Amen at 11:55. Ranch at 12:10.
credit: A Nathan Tabor / Nathan AI project

chapters.title: Hold Everything and Clear the Aisle
paras: At 11:55 the last amen still had a tail on it. By 12:10 Rev. Buford Gravywell was leaning over the sneeze guard like he had spotted the Promised Land in a pan of mashed potatoes. Lottie Mae had picked the table that left the aisle clear and worked out how to reach the hot yeast rolls before the next batch of folks in Sunday suits.

Buford preaches at Lonesome Gravy Fork Independent Baptist. Lottie Mae Gravywell is his wife. The Gravywells, the churches, and the buffet staff in these scenes are fictional. The server accounts at the end come from published interviews and firsthand posts.
Two plates each. One check. The pulpit gets forty-five minutes. The receipt gets the last word.

chapters.title: Buford Builds a Gravy Levee
paras: Plate one has three pieces of fried chicken, two scoops of mashed potatoes, two ladles of brown gravy, one scoop of fried okra, and two yeast rolls. Ten portions. First go the drumsticks, stood up like fence posts. He banks the potatoes against them and pours the gravy down the middle. The okra goes where the rim still shows.
He eats the chicken hot. One roll catches the gravy running toward his tie. The other sweeps up the bottom of the plate. He takes the first bite standing up because somebody wants to shake his hand.

Plate two has three slices of roast beef, two scoops of mac and cheese, one wedge of hot cornbread, one yeast roll, one dish of banana pudding, and one scoop of peach cobbler. Nine portions. He alternates beef and mac, sweeps up with the cornbread, and goes back and forth between pudding and cobbler. Nineteen portions across two plates.

chapters.title: Lottie Mae Works the Rim
paras: Plate one carries two slices of roast beef, two scoops of green beans, one scoop of mashed potatoes, one ladle of gravy, one scoop of fried okra, one wedge of hot cornbread, and one yeast roll. Nine portions. She sections off the beans, gives the potatoes the gravy, and takes a forkful from each side. She snaps the cornbread in half for the last of the gravy.

Plate two has two pieces of fried chicken, one scoop of mac and cheese, one scoop of creamed corn, one yeast roll, one dish of banana pudding, and two scoops of peach cobbler. Eight portions. She uses the roll to keep the corn from running into the pudding. The cobbler gets the dry rim and the last two bites.

Lottie Mae eats seventeen portions. She and Buford take thirty-six across four plates. Drinks have their own line on the server’s ticket. Lottie Mae slides the empty glasses to the aisle side and asks for both refills together.

chapters.title: The Fifteen-Top
paras: Della Jean Skillet has a fifteen-top, two trays of tea, and three versions of how long the ranch has been missing. Three people ask on three different trips. A fourth holds up a glass from the far side of the table. Somebody decides two minutes is a personal insult.

Combine the requests and give the kitchen time. Pull the chair out of the aisle. When you fold that imitation bill under a plate, the person lifting it gets one second of relief before the joke lands. There is still rent on the other side of that joke.

When the check comes in the story, it reads $36.00 before tax. One plus one equals two. Twenty percent of $36.00 is $7.20. The play receipt counts real cash or card tips. It records the imitation bill as zero.

chapters.title: Two-Mile Hatpin Takes a Seat
paras: Deacon Otis Taterknoll comes in from Two-Mile Hatpin Independent Baptist with a jacket full of peppermints and a story about the church van. He borrows a menu to check the tip. Lottie Mae asks him if he needs a calculator or a pencil. He turns the menu over and works it out in the margin.

Della Jean calls for hands because the cornbread is up and the church table has a chair in the aisle. Otis stands, pulls the chair in, and asks whether she can bring the refills together when she has a free hand. Buford is still talking. Lottie Mae is already out of the way.
The next table never heard the sermon. They saw the chair move, the server walk through, and a tip get written down. That took less time than the closing prayer.

chapters.title: Who I Am. Whom I Be. What I Bee.
paras: John Nathan Tabor. Preacher’s kid. IFB. KJV. Youngest of three boys. Owens Cross Roads, Alabama, and the Flint River are where Nathan puts the beginning of this story. Hooked on Phonics, McGuffey Readers, the King James Bible, television, movies, and music. In his family telling, Grandma Opal’s line was to play dumb until you know what you’re dealing with.

“Well, whatca need done—and when you need it done by?” That is the question Nathan brings to the table. Who I am is the PK who knows the cadence. Whom I be is the one looking to see who did the work. What I bee is the honey and the stinger. The honey is giving freely. The stinger is reading the receipt out loud. INNOCENCE IS NOT A COMMODITY.
“MY YES IS MY YES. MY NO IS MY NO. 1 + 1 = 2!” Nathan’s twenty-percent rule gets a dollar line. That is where the person who carried the plates can see it.

chapters.title: The KJV at the Check
paras: Proverbs 23:20–21 puts riotous eating and gluttony on the page. James 5:4 makes withheld wages cry out. 1 Timothy 5:18 says, “The labourer is worthy of his reward.” James 1:27 puts care for the fatherless and widows in plain view.

The hard question belongs at your own table. How did you speak to the person pouring the tea? How many times did you send them back? Was the paper under the plate money? Who put the room back in order after you left?
The preacher’s wife puts the card down before the preacher can fish for a tract. He looks at the total, takes a beat, and writes $7.20. They clear the aisle on the way out.

chapters.title: Send It to Your Framily and Friends
paras: AMEN AT 11:55. RANCH AT 12:10. Somebody at the table writes it on the back of a spare order slip. Buford says his card ought to say TWO LADLES. ONE GRAVY LEVEE. Lottie Mae puts her fork down long enough to answer: COBBLER GOES ON THE RIM.

Pick one of those cards in the game or write your own punch line. The Sunday Receipt card can show the tip from your last round. Save or share the PNG to keep the version you made. Send it to your framily and friends and see who can get both plates right.
Della Jean has a card of her own. It reads THE RECEIPT GETS THE LAST WORD.

chapters.title: Receipts From the Shift
paras: In a 2017 Christian Post opinion piece, Shane Pruitt printed accounts from servers who recalled demanding after-church tables, low tips and tracts left on the table. Jason Pierce’s essay draws on those same interviews. Treat the two articles as overlapping evidence.

In a 2019 r/Christianity discussion, a commenter recalled lower per-customer tips on Sundays while working as a server. Other commenters describe paper that looks like money. These accounts speak to individual experiences. The cited material gives neither a representative industry-wide ranking nor typical portion counts for IFB families.

U.S. Department of Labor Fact Sheet #15 describes the federal $2.13 direct cash wage where an employer lawfully uses a tip credit. The employer must make up a workweek shortfall against the applicable minimum. More protective state standards can apply.
